title: Ekattorer Dinguli (Days of '71)
author: Jahanara Imam
note: Iconic diary-style memoir chronicling war-time life, loss, and resistance through a mother's perspective.

title: Ami Birangona Bolchi (A War Heroine, I Speak)
author: Nilima Ibrahim
note: Groundbreaking testimonies of Birangonas documenting gendered violence during the war.

title: Muldhara '71
author: Maidul Hasan
note: Insider account of political and diplomatic strategy under the Tajuddin-led provisional government.

title: Rifle, Roti, Aurat
author: Anwar Pasha
note: War-time novel written during 1971, reflecting fear, violence, and collapse in occupied Dhaka.

title: Jochona O Jononir Golpo
author: Humayun Ahmed
note: Epic narrative weaving ordinary lives with major historical moments of the Liberation War.

title: Hangor Nodi Grenade
author: Selina Hossain
note: Powerful fiction of sacrifice, resistance, and moral crisis in a rural wartime setting.

title: The Rape of Bangladesh
author: Anthony Mascarenhas
note: Influential account that helped expose atrocities in East Pakistan to a global audience.

title: The Blood Telegram
author: Gary J. Bass
note: Detailed political history of U.S. policy, diplomatic cables, and the genocide context of 1971.

title: 1971: A Global History of the Creation of Bangladesh
author: Srinath Raghavan
note: Global perspective on the war across India, Pakistan, the U.S., USSR, and China.

title: Bondi Shibir Theke
author: Shamsur Rahman
note: Poetry from occupied Dhaka capturing fear, defiance, and resistance.

title: Payer Awaj Pawa Jai
author: Syed Shamsul Haq
note: Verse play set in the final days of the war, exploring collaborator psychology and collapse.

title: History of the 1971 Liberation War
author: Documentary Video
note: Documentary-style visual overview of 1971 events and context.
